reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a step-by-step Coinbase account, identity-verification, purchase, transfer, and security tutorial, while clearly disclosing referral links and affiliate compensation. It promotes ordinary cryptocurrency signup and trading actions with stated eligibility conditions for the Bitcoin bonus, but the supplied content does not show a deceptive claim, impersonation, or concealed money or data diversion.

opening.argument: The video ties a promised crypto reward directly to the viewer’s financial action: clicking the referral link, then buying or selling Bitcoin. The speaker also acknowledges receiving a kickback, so the offer simultaneously benefits the viewer and routes value to the promoter. That is a concrete reward-for-action solicitation, not merely general education. The description reinforces the same call to action by presenting a referral link as the way to start and advertising free BTC.

citations.quote: this link is going to give you 10 dollars worth of free bitcoin when you buy or sell 100 dollars of bitcoin it also gives me a kickback and supports this channel
CLICK THIS LINK TO START (for 10$ FREE BTC) ▶ https://tinyurl.com/yourfriendroberta (Referral Link)

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the steps a tutorial does not answer the reward linkage. The cited account, payment, and purchase instructions are precisely the actions the viewer must take to reach the advertised bonus. Nor does stating that a transaction is irreversible establish that the solicitation is ordinary or adequately explained. The important point is that the video places a crypto reward and the promoter’s compensation alongside a requested financial action.

citations.quote: this link is going to give you 10 dollars worth of free bitcoin when you buy or sell 100 dollars of bitcoin it also gives me a kickback and supports this channel

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quote establishes a disclosed referral incentive with an explicit purchase-or-sale condition, not a concealed diversion or false guarantee. The description also identifies the link as a referral link, while the video demonstrates the platform’s ordinary account and trading workflow. Those facts show a promotional tutorial with a conditional bonus, but do not show that the reward is unavailable or deceptive.

The description of this video contains affiliate links. This means that if you buy one of the products that I recommend, I’ll receive a small commission without any additional cost to you.

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals appear together: crypto rewards, referral destinations, additional signup bonuses, and a limited giveaway tied to engagement. The video says viewers need only like, comment, and subscribe for a chance at $50, limited to the first hundred subscribers. The description also advertises bonuses as high as $250 and $50 through other crypto services. Presented together, these offers create a strong low-barrier reward pitch that can draw viewers into multiple signup and transaction pathways.

citations.quote: All you need to do is like this video, comment and subscribe. And I will choose from the first hundred subscribers. One person to get $50 worth of Bitcoin.
BlockFi (up to $250 Signup Bonus) ► https://blockfi.com/?ref=9fa73887
Celsius ($50 Signup Bonus)►https://celsiusnetwork.app.link/1259323f66 (code: 1259323f66)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account treats each instruction in isolation and leaves out the accumulation of incentives. A time-limited $50 crypto giveaway, a referral bonus, and other signup bonuses are not necessary to explain how to use Coinbase. Their combination makes the presentation materially more solicitation-driven than a neutral operational demonstration, even without proving that every offer is false.

citations.quote: All you need to do is like this video, comment and subscribe. And I will choose from the first hundred subscribers. One person to get $50 worth of Bitcoin.
BlockFi (up to $250 Signup Bonus) ► https://blockfi.com/?ref=9fa73887

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are visible promotional conditions, not evidence of deception. The $50 item is expressly described as a selection from the first hundred subscribers, and the referral material identifies signup bonuses rather than promising investment profits. The supplied content does not show that any reward was withheld, that eligibility conditions were hidden, or that viewers were guaranteed a return.

opening.argument: Although framed as a beginner tutorial, the content functions as a promotional funnel. The title promises a complete Coinbase walkthrough, while the description directs viewers to referral links for free BTC and several other crypto services. The presenter actively tells viewers to click the link, explains the bonus, and discloses receiving a kickback. The instructional format therefore supplies practical steps that steer viewers toward account creation and transactions, with education serving the promotional pathway.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of real interface instructions does not make the surrounding solicitation neutral. The presenter does not merely describe Coinbase; she directs viewers to a particular signup link and lists multiple incentivized destinations. The reference opening’s account of verification and purchasing explains the mechanism of participation, but it does not rebut that the tutorial is being used to promote reward-linked actions.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial’s promotional aspect is openly disclosed rather than disguised as independent reporting. The description says affiliate compensation comes only if viewers buy a recommended product and states there is no additional cost, while also warning that the material is not financial advice. A disclosed referral tutorial can steer viewers without establishing a scam or an unavailable reward.
